title: Afternoon
description: Looking straight up from the corner of Honjo 3-chome in Tokyo on a February afternoon: the signal gantry and its street sign hang over you, the pole and the wires cross the sky, the building edges lean in, and a towering cumulus rises from behind the roofs on the right. The street is taken apart into what it is made of and lit again. Drag sideways to move the sun through the afternoon, from half past twelve to the last light at five. The faces turn toward and away from it, the pole and the signal heads throw their shadows across the walls, the low sun goes behind the buildings and leaves them in the blue of the open sky, the sky holds a deep cobalt overhead and opens to a warm white low down toward the sun, and the cumulus's sunlit flank goes from warm white to peach and its lit faces swing lower while its shade stays sky blue. At the photographer's own sun the street is the photograph.
intent: Reality pieces: depth maps and material maps, making a real place as real as possible but interactive. One photograph is baked into material maps (MoGe-2 metric depth and normals for a worm's-eye frame, the camera pitched 29 degrees up, true up from the vanishing point of the plumb building edges and the walls snapped to their azimuths around it; albedo by dividing out the shading of the photo's own sun, which is fitted to the walls; the sun mask of that light; a sky and cloud matte) and relit live: Lambert sun plus hemispheric sky about the true up, cast shadows by screen-space ray marching the depth toward a real solar position (Tokyo, 35.7 N, early February) plus exact capsule shadows for the pole, its lamp and the signal mast arm, and the sky drawn by an analytic clear-sky model (a cyan-cobalt zenith whose hue holds at every sun, lightening to a pale cobalt horizon, a warm band added only in the sun's azimuth once it is low, circumsolar glow) with a photographed cumulus plate (its own luminance and alpha) composited behind the roofs and the pole and relit by the same sun (lobe relief from its own coverage and tone, a warm-white sunlit side that rolls off under clipping, skylight-blue shade, a thin warm ring round its sunlit edge), then developed through the shared film kit. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsic_image_decomposition

sources.author: Patrick Beznoska (@patrick_beznoska)
sources.note: Tokyo (Honjo 3-chome, Sumida), published 5 February 2025; 5612x3741 original, shipped at 2400x1600. Metric depth, normals and field of view (70.7 degrees) from MoGe-2 ViT-S (Microsoft, MIT) via tools/depth/normals.py; sky matte via tools/depth/segment.py sky, corrected inside MoGe's surface mask; up from the plumb edges' vanishing point, wall snapping, the photo's sun fitted to the walls, its sun mask, albedo, cloud matte and the thin-occluder capsules baked by tools/depth/bakes/afternoon (bake.py, light.json, capsules.json) into albedo.webp, normal.png (octahedral normal, occluder thickness), depth.png (16-bit log depth, the photo's sun mask) and matte.png (sky; its cloud channel no longer drawn). Replaces the first plate, an eye-level intersection in Kyoto by Richard Tao (Unsplash, https://unsplash.com/photos/street-intersection-in-japanese-town-jlJFU9QBfFc).

sources.author: Dimitrios Savva (photography), Jarod Guest (processing), Poly Haven
sources.note: The cumulus: the HDRI's towering cumulus as the denchuka bake matted it (blue-excess key, unmixed from its sky, tone-mapped from linear radiance with a soft shoulder), cut out, its two contrail-like streaks filled and its lower body continued below the plate's cut by tools/depth/bakes/afternoon/cumulus.py into cloud.webp (grey luminance, alpha), laid on the frame with its foot behind the right-hand roofs, turned 22 degrees so it leans in toward the zenith with the building edges, and relit live.
